User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the GanttFlow application. This entity stores basic user information linked to an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The user's email address, typically provided by an external authentication system.

displayName.description: The user's preferred name for display within the application.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Project.title: Project
Project.description: Represents a major initiative or body of work that can be managed and visualized in the GanttFlow application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Project entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the project, providing context and scope, useful for the AI Task Assistant Tool.

startDate.description: The planned start date for the project.

endDate.description: The planned end date for the project.

ownerId.description: Reference to the User who created or owns this project. (Relationship: User 1:N Project)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.

Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents an individual task within a project, including its schedule, progress, and dependencies.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task entity.

projectId.description: Reference to the Project this task belongs to. (Relationship: Project 1:N Task)

name.description: The name or title of the task.

description.description: A detailed description of the task.

startDate.description: The planned start date for the task.

endDate.description: The planned end date for the task.

progressPercentage.description: The current completion percentage of the task (0-100).

status.description: The current status of the task.

predecessorTaskIds.description: An array of task IDs that must be completed before this task can start. (Relationship: Task N:N Task - self-referencing)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the task was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. Access is restricted to the user whose ID matches the document path. The '{userId}' parameter corresponds to the authenticated user's UID.

Contains projects created and owned by a specific user. Authorization is achieved through the hierarchical path: only the authenticated user matching '{userId}' can access their projects. This structure ensures Authorization Independence and supports QAPs for listing a user's projects.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this project.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the project.

definition.description: Stores tasks belonging to a specific project. Authorization is inherited from the parent project's path: only the authenticated user matching '{userId}' (the project owner) can access tasks within their projects. This structure ensures Authorization Independence for tasks, avoiding 'get()' calls to parent documents in security rules.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent project.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent project.

params.name: taskId
params.description: The unique identifier for the task.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for GanttFlow prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to path-based authorization and structural segregation. This approach ensures robust security rules and efficient queries, directly addressing the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, QAPs, and Invariants.

1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** User profiles are stored in a top-level collection `users`. Each user's document ID (`{userId}`) is directly tied to their Firebase Authentication UID. This immediately establishes ownership and privacy for user-specific data, as access rules can simply check `request.auth.uid == userId`.

2.  **Projects (`/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}`):** Projects are organized as a subcollection under the owning user's profile. This hierarchical path (`/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}`) is fundamental to achieving **Authorization Independence** and supporting **QAPs**.
    *   **Authorization Independence:** By nesting projects under `/users/{userId}`, access to a project is inherently tied to the authenticated user. Security rules for `projects/{projectId}` can directly verify `request.auth.uid == userId` (where `userId` is the path parameter) without needing to perform a `get()` operation on a parent user document or relying on an `ownerId` field *within* the project document itself for primary authorization. This avoids the pitfalls of hierarchical authorization dependencies, enabling atomic operations and simplifying rule debugging.
    *   **QAPs:** This structure enables efficient and secure listing of projects. A user can fetch all their projects by querying `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('projects')`. The rules will automatically enforce that only projects under the authenticated user's path can be read.

3.  **Tasks (`/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`):** Tasks are further nested as a subcollection under their respective projects. This continues the hierarchical authorization model.
    *   **Authorization Independence:** Similar to projects, task authorization is derived directly from its path. For a task at `/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`, the security rule `request.auth.uid == userId` (where `userId` is the path parameter representing the project owner) grants access without requiring any `get()` calls to the parent project's data. This design ensures that task access is atomic and independent of the parent document's *content* for authorization.
    *   The `Task` document includes `projectId` as per the schema, which is useful for cross-referencing or specific queries, but its primary authorization relies on the hierarchical path.
    *   **QAPs:** Listing tasks for a given project is straightforward and secure: `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('projects').doc(projectId).collection('tasks')`.

This structure provides a clear and predictable model where access control is primarily determined by the document's path, making Firestore security rules concise, easy to understand, and highly performant. The use of descriptive wildcards (`userId`, `projectId`, `taskId`) further enhances clarity and debuggability.
